senses.gloss: to be torn loose, be released. Y. Taan. II, 65ᵈ top, v. נָטַשׁ II a. נָתשׁ.—Trnsf. to be untied, released from an obligation; to become permitted. Y. Yeb. IV, 6ᵇ bot. (ref. to Deut. XXV, 10) בית שהוא נִיתָּר וכ׳ a house (of several wives) which is released (from the leviratical marriage) by means of one ḥălitsah (performed on one of the wives). Y. Bicc. I, 64ᵇ top כל הביכורים שנראו לִיתּוֹר … אינן נִיתּוֹרִין וכ׳ all the first fruits which are to be released (become permitted by being brought to the Temple) in the land (of Palestine), can become so only by reciting the confession (Deut. XXVI, 5—10).
units: <cite ref="Eruvin 10a">Erub. 10ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Eruvin 12a:9">12ᵃ</cite> <he>חצר נִיתֶּרֶת וכ׳</he> a court becomes permitted (for Sabbath purposes) by &c., v. <cite ref="Q01223"><he>פַּס</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Eruvin 12a:9">Ib.</cite> <he>שהוא נִיתָּר וכ׳</he> that it is made available &c.; a. e.

<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 16:5">Tosef. Sabb. XVI</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 17:5">XVII</cite>), 5 <he>שהִתִּירוֹ</he> which one unscrewed; <cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 20:5">Sabb. XX, 5</cite> <he>מַתִּירִין</he>, v. <cite ref="M01350"><he>מַכְבֵּשׁ</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 22a">Ib. 22ᵃ</cite> <he>מתירין</he> (<cite ref="R00440"><he>ציצית</he></cite>) <he>מבגד לבגד</he> you may untie show-fringes from one garment (and put them) on another garment.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 5:2">Gen. R. s. 5</cite> <he>מַתִּירָן ומוציא וכ׳</he> he unties them (opens the bags) and lets the air in them escape; a. fr.—[<cite ref="Tosefta Shevi'it 1:7">Tosef. Shebi. I, 7</cite>, v. <cite ref="F00115"><he>וָתַר</he></cite>.]

<cite ref="Shabbat 4a:9">Sabb. 4ᵃ</cite> <he>הִתִּירוּ לו וכ׳</he> would they (the scholars) permit him to take it out &c.? <cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 2:4">Ib. II, 4</cite> <he>ור׳ יהודה מַתִּיר</he> but R. Judah declares it permitted.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 2:2">Ib. 2</cite> <he>וחכמים מַתִּירִין</he>; a. v. fr.—V. <cite ref="M03064"><he>מַתִּיר</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 40b:19">Snh. 40ᵇ</cite> <he>ה׳ עצמו למיתה</he> did he surrender himself to death?, i.e. did he declare that he would commit the act in spite of the warning which defined it to be a deadly crime? <cite ref="Sanhedrin 41a:9">Ib. 41ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 17:6">Deut. XVII, 6</cite>) <he>עד שיַתִּיר וכ׳</he> until he declares himself ready to undergo capital punishment for his act.
<cite ref="Chullin 41a">Ḥull. 41ᵃ</cite>. Y. Peah I, 16ᵃ <he>עילא … להַתִּיר דמן וכ׳</he> they wanted a pretext to outlaw the rebels; a. fr.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 28">Lev. R. s. 28</cite>, beg., a. fr. <he>הוּתְּרָה הרצועה</he>, v. <cite ref="T00977"><he>רְצוּעָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 20:5">Sabb. XX, 5</cite> <he>אם היה מוּתָּר וכ׳</he> if it (the clothes press) was (partly) unscrewed on the eve of the Sabbath, he may unscrew it entirely.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 9b">B. Kam. 9ᵇ</cite> <he>שור מותר</he> an ox that is not tied, opp. <cite ref="S02226"><he>קשור</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Eruvin 2:1">Erub. II, 1</cite> <he>קשורות אבל לא מוּתָּרוֹת</he> closely tied together, but not tied in a loose way; a. e.

senses.gloss: to be permitted. Y. Sabb. II, 5ᵇ bot. ה׳ הנדר, v. נֶדֶר; Snh. 68ᵃ.
units: <cite ref="Chullin 17a">Ḥull. 17ᵃ</cite> <he>בתחילה ה׳ להן וכ׳</he> originally they were permitted to eat the flesh of an animal killed by stabbing (v. <cite ref="N00493"><he>נְחִירָה</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Chullin 9a:10">Ib. 9ᵃ</cite> <he>נשחטה הותרה</he> when the animal has been slaughtered according to the ritual, it is (absolutely) permitted.

Erub. 93ᵇ שבת כיון שהותרה הותרה as regards Sabbath laws what has been permitted at the entrance of the Sabbath remains permitted the entire day; ib. 70ᵇ כל שה׳ למקצת וכ׳ whatever is permitted for one part of the Sabbath &c.; a. v. fr.—Part. מוּתָּר; f. מוּתֶּרֶת; pl. מוּתָּרִים, מוּתָּרִין; מוּתָּרוֹת (it is, they are) permitted (of things and persons).
<cite ref="Mishnah Terumot 10:7">Ter. X, 7</cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Yevamot 1:2">Yeb. I, 2</cite> <he>צרתה מ׳</he> her rival is permitted (to him as wife).
<cite ref="Mishnah Yevamot 3:2">Ib. III, 2</cite> <he>ומ׳ באחותה</he> and he is permitted to marry her sister.
<cite ref="Mishnah Yevamot 2:10">Ib. II, 10</cite> <he>מותרות לינשא להן</he> may be married to them; a. v. fr.—
<cite ref="Pesachim 48a">Pes. 48ᵃ</cite>, a. e. (ref. to <he>ממשקה ישראל</he>, <cite ref="Ezekiel 45:15">Ez. XLV, 15</cite>) <he>מן המותר לישראל</he> of what an Israelite is permitted to drink.

<cite ref="Shabbat 108a:12">Sabb. 108ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <he>בפיך</he>, <cite ref="Exodus 13:9">Ex. XIII, 9</cite>) <he>מדבר המותר בפיך</he> the Torah must be written on the skin of an animal which is permitted in thy mouth (a clean animal).
